samples.summary: A style command over a range with an unresolvable endpoint (nested table) is now a silent, feedback-free no-op
samples.evidence: `visitRangeSlices` line 198: `if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;`. `getBlockIndex` searches only `getContextBlocks()`, so an endpoint inside a *nested* table normalizes (via `topLevelBlockId`/`anchorCI.tableBlockId`) to the inner table block, which is not a context block, and the function returns having visited nothing. Because `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (document.ts:361) is the sole write path, the user's Cmd+B / toolbar toggle over such a selection writes nothing at all, and `dirtyBlockIdsForRange` returns an empty set so no repaint is scheduled either — the command is silently dropped with no error and no UI signal. The previous code crashed with a `TypeError` on `contextBlocks[-1].type`, so this is a strict improvement in robustness, but it converts a loud failure into a silent data no-op. The new test `packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts` ('does not throw for an endpoint inside a nested table') pins exactly this behaviour, so it is intentional; flagging because a lost user edit with no feedback is still a correctness gap worth an explicit decision (e.g. falling back to a whole-cell write, or surfacing the unsupported case).

samples.summary: Spread of a per-row array into `Math.max` can throw RangeError on a pathologically large table
samples.evidence: `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1` spreads one argument per table row into `Math.max`. Engines cap the argument count (~64k–125k depending on the engine and stack state), so a table with that many rows raises `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` / `too many arguments` inside `visitCellRectangleSlices`, taking down both `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` (the cell-rectangle write) and `visitStyledRunsInRange`'s summary read. A `reduce` avoids the limit. Row counts that large are implausible for a document editor, hence nit, but the old code this replaced (editor.ts `applyStyleToCellRange`) had no such construct, so it is newly introduced.

finding.summary: Consolidated write path marks dirty by indexing body blocks with context-relative indices — wrong block or TypeError in header/footer
finding.evidence: `applyStyleToSelection` (new single write path for the B/I/U/S toggles, clear-formatting Cmd+\ and the format painter Cmd+Alt+V) computes `startIdx = this.doc.getBlockIndex(range.anchor.blockId)` / `endIdx = ...`. `Doc.getBlockIndex` resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:211-213), i.e. the *header* or *footer* block array when `doc.editContext !== 'body'`. The loop then dereferences `this.doc.document.blocks[i].id` — always the BODY array. In header/footer context the indices therefore address the wrong array: the wrong block is marked dirty (stale repaint) and, when the header/footer region has more blocks than the body, `document.blocks[i]` is `undefined` and `.id` throws a TypeError, aborting the render. The keyboard toggles and clear-formatting are reachable in header/footer (the slim header/footer toolbar exists in docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:387). Note this indexing pattern pre-dates the change (it was duplicated in the old `clearFormatting`/`toggleStyle` tails), but the change makes it the single shared path and did not fix it while explicitly reworking the surrounding dirty-marking (the `getCellInfo(anchor) ?? getCellInfo(focus)` fallback right above).

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present in `applyStyleToSelection`. That method (text-editor.ts:2921-2940) contains no `getBlockIndex` calls and no `document.blocks[i]` dereference: for a cell rectangle it marks `range.tableCellRange.blockId`, otherwise it marks dirty via `dirtyBlockIdsForRange(this.doc, range)` (line 2938). `dirtyBlockIdsForRange` (range-slices.ts:109-115) returns block *ids* from `visitRangeSlices`, whose top-level cross-block branch walks `doc.getContextBlocks()` (range-slices.ts:206) — the header/footer array when `editContext !== 'body'` — and guards with `if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` (line 198) and `if (!block) continue;` (line 209). So neither the wrong-block dirty-marking nor the `undefined.id` TypeError can occur on this path; the file comment at range-slices.ts:99-104 states this refactor exists precisely to retire that duplicated body-index arithmetic. The only surviving `getBlockIndex` → `this.doc.document.blocks[i]` pattern in text-editor.ts (lines 2273-2279) lives in `forEachBlockInSelection` (line 2230), a block-style (indent/alignment) helper that neither applies inline styles nor marks dirty — a different function from the one the finding names and describes. The equivalent toolbar helper in editor.ts:1344-1364 already uses `doc.getContextBlocks()`.
